title: icipe MaxEnt model maps desert locust breeding regions in East Africa with mean AUC up to 0.887
summary: Peer-reviewed MaxEnt model trained on 5,406 FAO breeding records (1985–2020) projected breeding suitability for Kenya, Uganda, South Sudan and Sudan; no operational outcome reported.
account: Researchers at the International Center of Insect Physiology and Ecology (icipe) used MaxEnt to predict desert locust breeding regions. The paper describes MaxEnt as a machine learning algorithm. Co-authors came from the Desert Locust Control Organization for Eastern Africa, Kenya's Plant Protection Services and FAO (Keith Cressman). Of 9,134 records accessed from FAO and the Moroccan anti-locust center, 5,406 breeding sites from Morocco (367), Mauritania (2,661) and Saudi Arabia (1,703) were used. They date from 1985–2020, with a 70/30 training-test split. The Mauritania model had the highest mean AUC (0.887), followed by Saudi Arabia (0.884) and Morocco (0.820). The models were projected to potential oviposition and breeding areas in Kenya, Uganda, South Sudan and Sudan. The authors thank DLCO-EA and Kenya's Ministry of Agriculture for field data. The paper does not report use of the predictions in control operations.
purpose: Predict regions suitable for desert locust breeding so that preventive control can be targeted before hoppers cause damage.
system: MaxEnt ecological-niche model of desert locust breeding (Kimathi et al.)
model_version: Maxent software, Version 3.4.1 (printed in the reference list as 'Version 3.4. 1')
developer: International Center of Insect Physiology and Ecology (icipe) with DLCO-EA, Kenya Plant Protection Services and FAO co-authors

ratings.reason: No use of the predictions by FAO, DLCO-EA or national control centers is documented in the paper.

ai_role.statement: The paper itself labels MaxEnt a machine learning algorithm and reports cross-validated AUCs. Nothing in the cited source shows that a forecast changed a survey or control decision.

fields.account: Researchers at the International Center of Insect Physiology and Ecology (icipe) used MaxEnt to predict desert locust breeding regions. The paper describes MaxEnt as a machine learning algorithm. Co-authors came from the Desert Locust Control Organization for Eastern Africa, Kenya's Plant Protection Services and FAO (Keith Cressman). Of 9,134 records accessed from FAO and the Moroccan anti-locust center, 5,406 breeding sites from Morocco (367), Mauritania (2,661) and Saudi Arabia (1,703) were used. They date from 1985–2020, with a 70/30 training-test split. The Mauritania model had the highest mean AUC (0.887), followed by Saudi Arabia (0.884) and Morocco (0.820). The models were projected to potential oviposition and breeding areas in Kenya, Uganda, South Sudan and Sudan. The authors thank DLCO-EA and Kenya's Ministry of Agriculture for field data. The paper does not report use of the predictions in control operations.
